task.request: Determine whether an unauthenticated external client can impersonate an arbitrary existing user in the actual deployment by sending a trusted-email header to POST /signin.

policySources.text: Trusted-header authentication is safe only when a trusted reverse proxy is the sole reachable ingress, removes any client-supplied identity header, and injects the authenticated identity itself.

acceptance.reason: The task author accepts the bounded policy without accepting any actual deployment fact.

principals.description: A client not authenticated by the trusted identity proxy that may control headers on an ingress it can reach.

resources.description: The identity and session of an existing user selected by the trusted-email header.

conditions.name: password-auth-signin-entry-enabled
conditions.basis: The supplied entry contains a password-auth sign-in gate.

conditions.name: trusted-email-header-name-configured
conditions.basis: The supplied environment source controls the header name.

conditions.name: email-authentication-produces-user
conditions.basis: The task concerns a session as a selected user.

conditions.name: deployment-ingress-enforces-header-trust
conditions.basis: The accepted policy requires exclusive trusted ingress and header replacement.

task.scopeAssurance: The fixed sources expose the application entry and configuration surface but do not supply actual deployment topology or configuration.
requiredAnalysis: separate source capability from actual deployment facts
constraints: Use only the supplied fixed context.

analysisRequirements.question: Which source-visible gates must be traversed before the trusted-email path can process the request?
How, if at all, does a request value become the identity used by this entry?
How is the selected identity bound to the existing-user session resource named by the obligation?
What source-visible application and accepted-policy controls decide whether this principal may obtain the selected user's session?
Under which source-visible branch can processing reach the protected session effect?
Which actual configuration, ingress, proxy, or authentication fact can change the deployment answer, and is it present in this fixed context?
If an optional provisioning branch is present, how does it affect identity binding before authentication?
